calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.7 expected goals per 60 against the Hurricanes.

calls.head: The Hurricanes like Hall’s line against Joseph’s
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Hall’s line (Hall, Jankowski and Robinson) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Oilers’ fourth line is Formenton, Michaels and Joseph.

calls.said: Rod Brind'Amour would send Hall, Jankowski and Robinson out against the Oilers’ fourth line again

calls.head: Who drives the play: the Hurricanes
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Oilers around the middle. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Oilers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.head: The Hurricanes roll four lines, the Oilers lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Hurricanes.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 70% chance, and they delivered.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton only a 30% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Edmonton couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Edmonton’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.9% (about 6.6% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Edmonton brought the hits
surprises.body: Edmonton’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 192, against their usual 107 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

story.head: Walker sparks a Hurricanes comeback
paras: Owen Michaels struck first for the Oilers midway through the first, and Leon Draisaitl made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. The Hurricanes scored five times in the second. Sean Walker got the Hurricanes on the board early in the second, and Mathieu Joseph pushed the lead to 3-1 shorthanded a little over three minutes later. The Oilers’ Zach Hyman left in the second period and didn’t return. Jalen Chatfield and Taylor Hall scored less than three minutes apart midway through the period to tie it 3-3. Andrei Svechnikov put the Hurricanes up 4-3 on the power play 43 seconds later. Vasily Podkolzin made it 4-4 for Edmonton on the power play less than five minutes later, but that was the last goal the Oilers would get. Sebastian Aho put the Hurricanes back ahead on the power play with 26 seconds left in the second. The Hurricanes’ Nikolaj Ehlers left early in the third period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Svechnikov scored again midway through the period to make it 6-4 for the Hurricanes. Alexander Nikishin stretched the lead to 7-4 on the power play with just over two minutes left. Aho finished with a goal and two assists.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Hurricanes win about four in five. Pyotr Kochetkov made 11 saves for the Hurricanes, and Devon Levi allowed seven goals on 36 shots.
The Hurricanes scored three power-play goals on six chances. The Canes moved to 17-3-3, still first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Oilers dropped to 17-5-3, still first in the Pacific.

items.text: Sebastian Aho passed Eric Staal for second on the Hurricanes’ all-time goals list, with 323.
Leon Draisaitl passed Mark Messier for third on the Oilers’ all-time assists list, with 643.
The Hurricanes have points in six straight games (5-0-1).
Connor McDavid extended his point streak against Carolina to eight games.
